vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: dr-context-pipeline
Version: 1.4.0

The dr-context-pipeline bundle implements a structured Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) workflow for agents, focusing on deterministic memory retrieval and context compression. The included Python scripts (install_pipeline.py, validate_pipeline.py, and memory_watchdog.py) perform standard file management, integrity hashing, and local file monitoring within the workspace without any network calls or unauthorized data access. The instructions in SKILL.md and the runtime checklists establish a rigorous 'evidence contract' that requires the agent to output transparent JSON artifacts, which serves as a defensive measure for correctness rather than a malicious prompt injection.

llm.summary: The skill is internally coherent with its stated purpose (a local, file-based deterministic context/retrieval pipeline); it only uses included Python scripts and workspace files and does not request unrelated credentials or remote installs.

dimensions.detail: Name/description align with the delivered assets: router, compressor prompt, JSON schemas, installer/validator/watchdog scripts, and tests. All required artifacts are local and appropriate for a memory retrieval+compression pipeline; nothing requires external credentials or unrelated capabilities.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md explicitly instructs the agent to read workspace memory files (memory/always_on.md and topic files), run installer/validator/watchdog scripts, and patch AGENTS.md while pasting command outputs. This is consistent with the purpose but the runtime evidence contract forces emission of Retrieval Bundle and Context Pack (including snippet texts and IDs) into the transcript; that may expose any sensitive content present in your memory files. Confirm the memory folder contents before applying.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No external install spec or network downloads; installer simply copies bundled assets into workspace. Scripts are plain Python and operate on local files. This is low-risk compared to URL downloads or registry installs.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requests no environment variables, secrets, or external credentials. The only data access is to workspace files (memory/, AGENTS.md, context_pipeline/) which is expected for this functionality.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always is false and autonomous invocation is default. The skill modifies only workspace files (context_pipeline/ installation and AGENTS.md) and does not alter other skills or system-wide agent settings. This level of persistence is reasonable for a workspace-local pipeline.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to do what it claims and uses only local scripts and files, but be aware: the apply flow and runtime contract require the agent to read and emit retrieval snippets (full snippet text and IDs) and to show command outputs and diffs. Before installing/applying: (1) inspect your memory/ directory and AGENTS.md for any secrets or sensitive information you don't want printed into transcripts or model inputs; (2) run the included scripts manually in a safe environment to review their outputs (install_pipeline.py copies assets, validate_pipeline.py checks hashes and JSON, memory_watchdog.py checks daily logs); (3) review the git diff produced for AGENTS.md before committing; (4) if you want a lighter interaction, explicitly waive the runtime evidence contract or run the pipeline locally yourself. If you want, I can highlight exactly which files will be copied and show the installer/validator/watchdog behavior in a simulated run (no real file ops) or help you scan your memory files for sensitive content first.
